title: Homelessness funding requests and interim housing update
subtitle: Paramedic alternate destination clinic, Erbs Road cabin shelter progress, encampment motion withdrawn, dental program report received.
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee recommended adding money to the preliminary 2023 homelessness budget to respond to funding requests from housing-system agencies {{vote:m1}}. The amount is $1,200,000 in 2023, rising to $1,800,000 in 2024. Staff will review the requests and report back with funding recommendations. The matter goes to the Strategic Planning and Budget Committee on February 22, 2023. Staff estimated the full $1.8 million could add about 0.3% to the tax rate, and said any ongoing cost would likely come from the property tax levy.
A motion to defer the matter was defeated. The committee also directed staff to build a formal process for the 2024 budget to consider such requests, with a diversity, equity and inclusion lens.

The committee also heard that the Region plans to seek provincial approval for an alternate destination clinic for mental health and addictions patients. It received a verbal update on the 50-cabin Erbs Road interim shelter, which staff are targeting for the end of March without guaranteeing a date. It also approved the consent agenda {{vote:m2}}, which included a Public Health dental program report. A notice of motion on encampment evictions was withdrawn.

decisions.item: Community funding requests in the housing stability system
decisions.detail: The committee recommended adding $1,200,000 to the preliminary 2023 homelessness budget and $1,800,000 in 2024, with staff to vet requests and report back, and forwarded this to the February 22 budget committee.
The committee received the consent agenda items for information and approved them, including the Public Health dental program updates report.

debate: Several councillors worried that many requests had not been vetted, may be out of date, or did not come through the budget process. One said ongoing money would be hard to reverse once added, and another questioned whether one agency's request was too large a share of the total.

Others said the need is clear and growing, and that staff should have a funding envelope so they can assess requests across the region. One councillor said some requests, such as support for A Better Tent City, were essential to keep existing services going.

Staff said they could not fully vet the requests before February 22 and that adding money would not guarantee any request is funded. Finance staff said ongoing costs would need the property tax levy, and that finding $2 million in offsets would mean service reductions.
Councillors raised fairness: agencies that did not ask during 2022 could be disadvantaged. This led to the direction to create a formal funding-request process for the 2024 budget.

On the Erbs Road shelter, one councillor pressed for clearer timing and interim options for the community space. Staff said moving residents into an unfinished construction site would be unsafe and undignified, and gave end of March as a target only.
